subject: [Bugfix] Fix a couple PPLX+CUTLASS MoE bugs (#20825)
pr_body:
Fix two bugs that prevented CUTLASS MoE to run with PPLX:

1. PPLX's All To All dispatch and combine functions require `topk_ids` to have the type `uint32`. Since we never expect elements of `topk_ids` to be negative when running with PPLX, this can be resolved with reinterpret casting the current signed `int32` type to unsigned.
2. CUTLASS MoE can be run from `compressed_tensors.py` either with PPLX or without it. If we run with PPLX, we end up running `CutlassExpertsFp8`'s forward function which takes different arguments than a straightforward non-PPLX `cutlass_moe_fp8` call. On the current main, this results in errors when running with PPLX. Fixing this issue also makes it easier to bring back pre-computed strides in [PR20762](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/20762).

#### Testing:

PPLX run:
```
export MASTER_ADDR=127.0.0.1
export MASTER_PORT=29500
export VLLM_ALL2ALL_BACKEND=pplx
python3 examples/offline_inference/data_parallel.py \
        --model="nm-testing/DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8" \
        --dp-size=2 \
        --tp-size=1 \
        --trust-remote-code
```

Non-PPLX run: run inference with `LLM(model="nm-testing/DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8")`

subject: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Register the offload region in chunks (#51081)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #51080.

`pin_mmap_region` registered the whole offload region with one `cudaHostRegister` call. A single registration of 512 GiB or more fails with `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` no matter how much host memory is free, so `cpu_bytes_to_use` at or above ~550e9 is never pinned. Measured on 4×H200 NVL with 1.3 TB free, one process, no model loaded:

| region size | result |
|---|---|
| 20 / 300 / 400 / 500 GB | success, ~0.1 s per GB |
| 549.7e9 (511.96 GiB) | success, 55.4 s |
| 549.9e9 (512.15 GiB) | **fails, code=2** |
| 600e9 | fails, code=2 |

This became reachable with #50094: before it each rank pinned its own `cpu_bytes_to_use / world_size` buffer, all far below the ceiling; after it one shared region is registered in full by every rank.

A failed registration also leaves its error pending on the thread, and the next error check in torch reports it against an unrelated call. That is how this surfaced for us: a bogus `AcceleratorError: CUDA error: out of memory` in `warm_v1_block_table_kernels`, and a worker that did not start.

## Changes

- Register the region in chunks of at most 64 GiB that end on block-row boundaries. Rows are page aligned, so the driver's page rounding never makes two registrations overlap and no block transfer spans a boundary. A single row larger than the cap is registered whole.
- Registration is all or nothing. On a failed chunk, drain the pending error and unregister the chunks registered before it, so `region.is_pinned` means the whole region is pinned. The cost is that a failure on the last chunk leaves the whole region on the pageable path; in exchange nothing downstream has to track a partly pinned region.
- Register, drain and roll back through one `CudaRTLibrary` instance. `torch.cuda.cudart()` has no `cudaGetLastError` binding, so the drain cannot go through torch. `CudaRTLibrary` gains `cudaHostRegister`, `cudaHostUnregister` and `cudaGetLastError` with their HIP names; this part comes from #50070 and its author is credited as co-author. If the runtime library cannot be loaded, the region stays pageable instead of failing worker startup.
- Cleanup of a fully registered region is unchanged: it releases `pinn …[truncated]

subject: [Bugfix][Kernel] Correct FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE tuning token bound (#46838)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Previously, #34542 refactored the FlashInfer CUTLASS fused MoE backend and passed the CUDA graph max capture size (typically 512) as `tune_max_num_tokens` for flashinfer_cutlass_fused_moe. However, `max_capture_size` describes graph capture capacity and can be unrelated to the scheduler/MoE max batched token limit, so using it can select a tuning configuration for the wrong token range and thus cause suboptimal perf unexpectedly.

This PR partially reverts #34542 and leaves `tune_max_num_tokens` as the default value (8192 defined in FlashInfer). Conceptually, the best value for `tune_max_num_tokens` is `FusedMoEConfig.max_num_tokens * parallel_factor`, but the parallel factor can vary across different parallel configurations and erroneous to determine (as pointed out in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46838#issuecomment-4834365663)), so we currently leave it as default, which is the behavior before #34542.

### Related Issue

This is part of the effort for #41306 to fix FlashInfer Cutlass fused MoE perf regression. There are also ongoing FlashInfer side fixes and optimizations to improve the MoE perf.

subject: [WideEP] Fix nvfp4 DeepEP High Throughput All2All backend (#33738)
pr_body:
## Purpose

On current main, `nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-NVFP4` crashes when used with the DeepEP high throughput all2all backend.

```
  NotImplementedError
    File "vllm/distributed/device_communicators/all2all.py", line 355, in dispatch_router_logits
      raise NotImplementedError
```

This PR fixes the issue by rejecting the FLASHINFER_TRTLLM backend in this case.

Details: `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` is a monolithic kernel that requires `dispatch_router_logits()` for the naive dispatch/combine path. However, `DeepEPHTAll2AllManager` only implements `dispatch()` for the modular kernel interfac, but not `dispatch_router_logits()`.

This fix causes backend selection to fall through to `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS`.

subject: [Bugfix][ROCm] Fix ViT rotary embeddings for torch.compile compatibility on ROCm (#27748)

## Purpose

This pull request updates the selection of rotary embedding function previously selected for the ROCm platform from `flash_attn.ops.triton.rotary` because it is not compatible with `torch.compile`. Since [this PR](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/23207) enabled `torch.compile` support for Qwen-VL models, it became necessary to address this incompatibility. After registering the rotary embedding operation using `direct_register_custom_ops` within vLLM, benchmarking revealed that the naive PyTorch implementation of the rotary embedding is actually faster on ROCm. subject: [Bugfix] Fix int32 destination offset overflow in CUTLASS MoE pre-reorder (#35188)
pr_body: ## Motivation `pre_reorder_triton_kernel_for_cutlass_moe` loads `dst_idx` from the `src2dst` mapping as an `int32` and uses it to calculate the destination address: ```python dst_ptr_offs + dst_idx * hidden_size ``` Because `dst_idx` is 32-bit, `dst_idx * hidden_size` can overflow signed 32-bit arithmetic when the destination activation buffer contains more than `2**31` elements. For example, with `hidden_size = 6144`, the first overflowing destination row is: ```text ceil(2**31 / 6144) = 349,526 ``` This is reachable during large expert-parallel prefill workloads. The wrapped offset can cause a CUDA illegal memory access or write to an incorrect GPU address. ## Modifications Promote `dst_idx` to `tl.int64` immediately after loading it: ```python dst_idx = tl.load(token_src2dst_ptr + idx).to(tl.int64) ``` This ensures that the multiplication by `hidden_size` and the destination pointer offset are evaluated using 64-bit arithmetic. The `src2dst` mapping remains `int32`; only the address calculation is widened. ## Accuracy Tests The change only affects destination address arithmetic. Outputs below the signed 32-bit offset boundary remain unchanged. The overflow boundary can be validated with an FP8 destination buffer using: - `hidden_size = 6144` - `dst_idx = 349,526` - A destination element offset greater than `2**31` - One BF16 input row converted and written to the selected FP8 row Expected behavior: - Before the fix: CUDA illegal memory access or an incorrect destination write. - After the fix: the selected destination row matches the FP8-converted input row. Large-offset validation requires a CUDA GPU with enough memory for a contiguous allocation larger than 2 GiB. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not benchmarked. The change adds one scalar `int32`-to-`int64` conversion for each valid routed destination. It does not change the number of loads, stores, kernel launches, or transferred elements.

subject: [ROCm] Fix QuickReduce fp16 saturation corrupting bf16 all-reduces (106M non-finite -> 0, +0.3%) (#34484)
pr_body:
Fixes #34473.

## Summary

QuickReduce converts BF16 inputs to FP16 before reduction for performance. GPT-OSS reaches magnitudes above FP16's maximum finite value (65,504), so the conversion could produce `inf`; quantized codecs then propagated that value through a 32-element block.

This PR:

- Enables `MODE.FP16_OVFL` on both gfx942 and gfx950 so FP16 overflow clamps instead of becoming non-finite.
- Uses a power-of-two range guard (`S = 16`) for `CodecFP`, scaling in FP32 before narrowing and restoring the scale on output.
- Emits `v_cvt_pk_f16_f32` explicitly for the scaled `CodecFP` conversion. This prevents LLVM from moving the FP16 conversion ahead of the scale.
- Keeps `CodecQ4/Q6/Q8` at `S = 1` on the existing fast FP16 path. Their block scaling already normalizes values, and a larger cast scale moves the reciprocal-scale saturation cliff into real data.
- Adds a four-GPU regression test covering low values, ordinary values, sums above FP16 range, individual inputs above FP16 range, negative overflow, and mixed blocks.

## Scope

This fixes the GPT-OSS non-finite-output failure without routing quantized codecs through native BF16 kernels. Quantized reductions may still clamp finite values when their FP16 accumulator exceeds 65,504; that is pre-existing lossy behavior and is intentionally left unchanged here. The native-BF16 alternative was numerically exact but 22–46% slower.

## Validation

- Built and passed the TP4 range regression on MI350X and MI355X with ROCm 7.2.
- `CodecFP` is bit-exact for all tested cases, including inputs and sums above FP16 range.
- Quantized codecs remain bit-exact for low and ordinary values and produce finite outputs for overflow cases.
- Captured GPT-OSS reductions went from non-finite outputs to zero non-finite outputs.
- PR-base versus final-patch latency on MI350X showed no measurable regression:
  - INT8/INT6/INT4: within 0.4% at 16 MiB and within 0.1% at 90 MiB.
  - FP: 9.6% faster at 16 MiB and 1.1% faster at 90 MiB in this run.
- Repository pre-commit checks pass.

## Test plan

---

linked_issues.title: [ROCm] QuickReduce bf16→fp16 cast corrupts gpt-oss-120b residuals: 62.7M non-finite elements on the default config
linked_issues.body:
## Summary

On MI350X (gfx950) with the official ROCm image, **gpt-oss-120b at TP4 produces 62.7 million non-finite elements in its residual stream under the default configuration**. The inputs are 100% finite — the corruption is created by the all-reduce.

The cause is that all-reduces above 64 MiB fall through to QuickReduce, which casts bf16 → **fp16** (max 65,504) before block-quantizing. gpt-oss's reduced activations reach **333,824**, overshooting the ceiling by **5.1×**.

This is the default path, not an opt-in one.

subject: Fix: Dynamic RoPE Cache Expansion to Prevent Position-ID Out-of-Bounds in EAGLE + Long-Sequence Workloads (#10788)
pr_body:
### **Title**

Fix: Dynamic RoPE Cache Expansion to Prevent Position-ID Out-of-Bounds in EAGLE + Long-Sequence Workloads

---

### **Background**

Running SGLang with **EAGLE speculative decoding** and long sequences occasionally triggers

```
RuntimeError: BatchQKApplyRotaryPosIdsCosSinCache failed with error code an illegal memory access was encountered
```

Root cause analysis shows that the crash occurs **whenever a generated `position_id` exceeds the length of the RoPE `cos_sin_cache` tensor**, which is initialized to `max_position_embeddings`.

* Mismatch between the target and draft model’s `max_position_embeddings` increases the likelihood, the *fundamental* issue is that the cache can be too short for real runtime positions, especially with speculative multi-step decoding and batching.

---

### **What This PR Does**

* **Thread-Safe Dynamic Expansion**

  * Adds `_ensure_cos_sin_cache_length()` to `RotaryEmbedding` for on-demand, cache growth.

* **Device-Aware Initialization**

  * Builds initial `cos_sin_cache` directly on the current CUDA device to prevent CPU–GPU copy overhead.

---

### **Expansion Policy**

The recommended pre-expansion formula (handled in the model runner before graph capture) is:

```
reserve_len = max(target_max_pos, draft_max_pos)
            + speculative_num_steps * speculative_num_draft_tokens
            + safety_margin  # (~1k)
```

This covers:

* Target/draft model declared maxima,
* Multi-step speculative decoding,
* A configurable buffer for future changes.

---

### **Results & Verification**

* Stress-tested with **1,200+ input tokens**, `speculative_num_steps=5`, and high concurrency.
* No illegal memory access observed.
* Single, one-time memory allocation; no runtime re-allocations during inference.
* Negligible performance impact—graph capture proceeds without synchronization penalties.

---

### **Why This Matters**

Any under-provisioned RoPE cache will still break under long or speculative workloads.
This PR makes SGLang **robust regardless of model mismatch** and future-proofs against larger context windows.

---

subject: [Bugfix] Support -1 (invalid/non-local) slots in topk_ids for Triton MoE (#46408)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Under expert parallelism, dispatch hands the experts a `topk_ids` tensor whose entries can be `-1`, marking invalid / non-local slots (a token's routed expert lives on another rank). The Triton unfused MoE path (`gpt_oss_triton_kernels_moe.py`) mishandled these in two places:

1. **`expert_map[topk_ids]`** (global→local remap) indexed the map with `-1`, which wraps to `expert_map[-1]` — a valid local id — and misroutes the slot. Replaced with a fused `remap_topk_to_local` kernel that preserves `-1` (the skip sentinel `make_routing_data` expects).
2. **`ops.moe_sum`** reduced over all `topk` slots, but `matmul_ogs` leaves the `-1` (non-local) slots **unwritten** in the intermediate buffer, so the sum folded in uninitialized garbage (and was NaN-unsafe). Replaced with a `masked_moe_sum` kernel that skips `-1` slots in the per-token reduction.

Both replace prior multi-op sequences with a single fused kernel. The now-unused `from vllm import _custom_ops as ops` import and the `moe_sum` wrapper are removed.

For the non-EP case (`expert_map is None`, no `-1`), behavior is unchanged: `remap_topk_to_local` is not called, and `masked_moe_sum` over all-valid slots equals the previous `moe_sum`.

### Naming note
`remap_topk_to_local` is deliberately **not** named `apply_expert_map`: a scalar `@triton.jit` device helper `apply_expert_map(expert_id, expert_map)` already exists in `deep_gemm_utils.py` (tested by #46061). This kernel is a different thing — a launchable, vectorized remap over a whole `topk_ids` tensor — so it gets a distinct name.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for `masked_moe_sum`, `apply_expert_map`, `expert_map topk_ids`. #46061 only adds a unit test for the existing DeepGemm device helper; #42034 fixes a padding sentinel in the FlashInfer one-sided path (different backend). Neither addresses `-1` handling in the Triton unfused path.

## Test plan

- Lint/type: `ruff check`, `ruff format`, `mypy` (via pre-commit) pass on the touched file.
- Functional: DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GB200 ×4, `dp=4 -ep`, Triton MoE backend with EP dispatch producing `-1` slots — GSM8K ~95%. Without this fix the path produces garbage output (mis-mapped `-1` and garb …[truncated]

subject: [Bugfix] Fix CPU split-KV scratchpad sizing (#45844)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix a CPU split-KV hang seen with `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`.

The worker could get stuck in `reduce_splits` waiting for a split completion flag. The root cause was the split-KV scratchpad was sized using the final output element size / smaller fallback q-head count, while the runtime split path writes temporary split outputs as `float` and can process more q-heads per split.

This could under-size the split-KV reduction buffer and allow split output data to overlap nearby reduction state, including split completion flags. As a result, `reduce_splits` could wait forever.

This PR sizes the relevant temporary outputs as `float` and sizes the split-KV reduction scratchpad using the maximum q-head tile the runtime can use.

## Test Plan

Test CPU throughput benchmark for `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`

```

subject: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fix batch invariance in RMSNorm kernels by pinning block size (#48391)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix a batch-invariance gap in the `fused_add_rms_norm` CUDA kernel.

The kernel selects its block size from the token count: `max_block_size = (num_tokens < 256) ? 1024 : 256`, independent of whether batch-invariant mode is enabled. Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the residual RMSNorm path (`RMSNorm.forward_cuda` with a residual → `ops.fused_add_rms_norm`) routes to this kernel. As a result the *same* token reduces with `block=1024` when processed in a small batch (`num_tokens < 256`) but with `block=256` inside a batch of `>= 256` tokens. The two block sizes give different `cub::BlockReduce` partitions and therefore a different fp32 sum-of-squares order, so the normalized output is not bit-exact across batch sizes whenever
`hidden_size > 256`.

The existing `batch_invariant_launch` flag only disabled vectorization (width 8 → 0); it did not touch the block size. This PR locks `max_block_size` to 1024 when `vllm_is_batch_invariant()` is true, making the reduction width independent of `num_tokens`.

This is a follow-up to #40413 (which routed the residual path to `fused_add_rms_norm` on the assumption it is already batch-invariant) and is tracked under #27433. It is not a duplicate: no open PR addresses the block-size-vs-`num_tokens` gap; #40413's test only compared `num_tokens=1` vs `4`, both below the 256 threshold, so it could not catch this.

## Test

**Both runs use this PR's updated test** (`test_fused_add_rms_norm_batch_invariant_residual_path`, the seed-swept version). The previous single-seed test (`seed=42`) passes on the buggy kernel, which is why it never caught this.
The decisive parameter is `n_extra`: `n_extra=299` makes `num_tokens=300 >= 256` (crossing the block-size threshold and exposing the bug), while `n_extra=3` (`num_tokens=4`) stays below it. That is why every failure below is an
`n_extra=299` case, and the seed is swept so a single lucky seed can't hide it.

- `n_extra=299` → `num_tokens = 300 >= 256`, so that same token now reduces with `block=256` — **crossing the threshold** and exposing the bug.
- `n_extra=3` → `num_tokens = 4 < 256`, stays at `block=1024`, so no divergence.

subject: [CI][AMD][BugFix] Update wvSplitK (and other skinny_gemm wrappers) to ensure tensors passed will be made contiguous for the kernel (#32831)
pr_body:
## Purpose
The `wvSplitKQ_hf_sml` kernel is not able to properly handle non-contiguous tensors.  This is resulting in failures in AMD CI.  This is possibly resulting in other failures or inaccuracies.  In the long term, it might be better to update the kernel to be able to properly handle non-contiguous tensors, since this trades incorrectness for performance loss. We can then work on fix  to the kernels in skinny_gems.cu to handle non-contiguous kernels.

In addition, all of the kernels in `skinny_gems.cu` are not able to handle tensors that return `is_contiguous()` as False.  The tensors may be contiguous in memory, but the kernels in skinny_gems.cu would need to be able to take strides as inputs.  The kernels in skinny_gems.cu are also susceptible to integer overflow if the tensor is too large. This may be fixable, but it will take more time to do this.

I have also updated the Python wrapper for the other kernels in this file to ensure that tensors passed to those kernels are made contiguous and issue a warning if a contiguous tensor is actually encountered, since it will usually result in a performance loss (and possibly a substantial one).

`pytest -sv models/language/generation/test_hybrid.py`
